Summarize the following text in exactly three bullet points. Preserve all important technical constraints.

A company is evaluating three language models hosted in Microsoft Foundry. The application sends prompts directly to each deployment without agents, tools, retrieval, or conversation memory. The evaluation must compare client-observed latency, time to first token, input tokens, output tokens, estimated cost, retries, and errors. The same prompts and output limits must be used for every model.

Summarize the following architecture decision as: Decision, Rationale, Risks, and Validation Plan.

The team will collect token usage from every SDK response and store it with a prompt ID and model deployment name. Azure Monitor metrics will be queried after each benchmark window to validate aggregate usage. Application Insights custom spans will correlate individual prompt executions. Cost will initially be estimated from a versioned price table because billing records are not expected to be immediately available.

Using only the information in this prompt, answer the question in one sentence.

Calculate the estimated request cost. Input price is €0.40 per million tokens. Output price is €1.20 per million tokens. The request used 2,500 input tokens and 600 output tokens. Show the formula and round the final answer to six decimal places.

Read the following synthetic operational report and return: one executive summary paragraph, three risks, and three actions.

During the evaluation window, the platform processed 12,000 requests across three model deployments. Most requests were short classification and extraction tasks. Two deployments remained below the target median latency, but one experienced intermittent throttling during the highest-concurrency test. The team discovered that retries were included in client elapsed time but were not counted as separate logical requests in the first report. Token totals from SDK responses were within the same general range as the Azure Monitor aggregates, although the observation windows were not aligned exactly. The cost calculation used a manually maintained pricing file whose effective date had not been recorded. No customer data was used, and all prompts were synthetic. The next run should align UTC query windows, record every physical attempt, version the pricing source, and separate sequential latency tests from concurrent throughput tests.
